alternate_names: Sri Stambadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple

history.summary: Sri Stambadri (Sthambadri) Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, on the Narasimha Swami Gutta hill in Khammam town — the best-supported in-town referent for this CSV row, and the most-reviewed Hindu temple in Khammam (4.8 stars, ~478 reviews, top-rated.online, consulted 2026-09-28). The one detailed web account (Velpu.com) describes a 3-tier Rajagopuram and a 32-pillared mandapam and attributes the temple's construction to the Kakatiya ruler Prathapa Rudra in the 16th century, after his darshanam of the lord — this is a single-source claim, not corroborated elsewhere, so the founding date is flagged as unverified. Khammam's name itself is linked to 'Stambadri/Kambham Mettu', the pillar-hill this temple stands on. Alternative district candidate: the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple at Garlavoddu village, Enkuru mandal (~45 km from Khammam town), also in Khammam district; this file documents the in-town Stambadri shrine as the best-supported match for a 'Khammam'-town row. No connection to the more famous Yadagirigutta (Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district) or Mattapalli (~150 km away) shrines — those are outside Khammam district. CSV town (Khammam), district (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are all correct — no correction needed.

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Stambadri, Khammam)
town_description: Khammam is a city and the district headquarters of Khammam district, Telangana, on the Munneru river, about 193 km east of Hyderabad. Its name is traditionally linked to 'Stambadri' or 'Kambham Mettu' — the hill of the pillar — the very Narasimha Swamy Gutta on which this temple stands. The city is known for the 950 AD Kakatiya-era Khammam Fort.
